title: HAVING, and the order SQL runs things in
explanation: WHERE filters rows BEFORE they're grouped. HAVING filters groups AFTER they're made. So if you want 'genres with more than 1 game', you need HAVING, because the count only exists after grouping. Here's the secret order SQL actually runs things in: FROM (find the table), WHERE (filter rows), GROUP BY (make groups), HAVING (filter groups), SELECT (pick columns), ORDER BY (sort), LIMIT (cut). That's why you can't use COUNT() inside WHERE: the groups don't exist yet!

example.code:
SELECT genre, COUNT(*) AS num_games
FROM games
GROUP BY genre
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2;

lines.explain: Show each genre and how many games it has.
Only keep groups with 2 or more games. HAVING is like WHERE, but for groups.

tasks.prompt: Show each genre with more than 1 game, and its count (call it num_games).
tasks.answer: SELECT genre, COUNT(*) AS num_games FROM games GROUP BY genre HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
hints: Group by genre, then filter the groups with HAVING.

solution_lines.explain: Show each genre and its count.
From the games table.
Make one group per genre.
Only keep genres with more than 1 game.

tasks.prompt: Show each genre whose cheapest game costs more than 30, with that cheapest price (call it cheapest).
tasks.answer: SELECT genre, MIN(price) AS cheapest FROM games GROUP BY genre HAVING MIN(price) > 30;
hints: Use MIN(price) in both the SELECT and the HAVING.

solution_lines.explain: Show each genre and its lowest price.
From the games table.
Make one group per genre.
Only keep genres where even the cheapest game costs more than 30.

tasks.prompt: Looking only at games released in 2015 or later, show each release year that has 2 or more games, with the count (call it num_games).
tasks.answer: SELECT release_year, COUNT(*) AS num_games FROM games WHERE release_year >= 2015 GROUP BY release_year HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2;
hints: You need BOTH: WHERE to filter the rows first, and HAVING to filter the groups after.
WHERE release_year >= 2015 GROUP BY release_year HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2

solution_lines.explain: Show each year and its count.
From the games table.
Step 1: throw away rows for games before 2015.
Step 2: group what's left by year.
Step 3: only keep years with 2 or more games.

tasks.prompt: Show each genre where all its games together cost more than 70. Show the total rounded to 2 decimals (call it total_cost), biggest total first.
tasks.answer: SELECT genre, ROUND(SUM(price), 2) AS total_cost FROM games GROUP BY genre HAVING SUM(price) > 70 ORDER BY total_cost DESC;
hints: Use SUM in the SELECT and the HAVING, then sort. ROUND is from Lesson 9.
SELECT genre, ROUND(SUM(price), 2) AS total_cost ... GROUP BY genre HAVING SUM(price) > 70 ORDER BY total_cost DESC

solution_lines.explain: Show each genre and the total of its prices, rounded.
From the games table.
Make one group per genre.
Only keep genres whose prices add up to more than 70.
Sort by the total, biggest first. ORDER BY runs after SELECT, so the nickname works here.

tasks.prompt: Predict first: which part of this query does SQL actually run FIRST?
tasks.code:
SELECT genre, COUNT(*) AS num_games
FROM games
WHERE price > 0
GROUP BY genre
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2
ORDER BY num_games DESC;
hints: You write SELECT first, but that's not the order SQL runs it in.
Before SQL can do anything, it has to know which table to look at.

solution_lines.explain: 1st: find the table.
2nd: throw away the free games.
3rd: make one group per genre.
4th: keep only genres with 2 or more paid games.
5th: pick the columns to show.
6th: sort the results.

recap: You just learned that WHERE filters rows before grouping, HAVING filters groups after, and SQL runs in this order: FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, SELECT, ORDER BY, LIMIT.
